classification.difficultyReason: Use supplementary co-interior angles to establish four right angles and apply the definition of a rectangle.

content.prompt: Prove that if a parallelogram has one right angle then it is a rectangle.

answer.short: Adjacent angles of a parallelogram are supplementary. Starting with one right angle therefore gives four right angles, so the parallelogram is a rectangle.
answer.worked:
Let $ABCD$ be a parallelogram with $\angle A=90^\circ$. Since $AB\parallel DC$ and $AD\parallel BC$, successive co-interior angles are supplementary.
$$\begin{align*}\angle B&=180^\circ-\angle A\\\angle B&=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\\\angle C&=180^\circ-\angle B\\\angle C&=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\\\angle D&=180^\circ-\angle C\\\angle D&=180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\end{align*}$$
All four angles are right angles. Hence $ABCD$ is a rectangle by definition.
